title: Rabi' al-Awwal: love of the Prophet ﷺ
hook: a month to study his life, celebrated or not
tomorrow: a gift brought down from the highest night. what was it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, rescue and grief: one day, two memories, carried in a glass of water. Today, a whole month, and a family question about love.

Some families throw a birthday party with a cake and a playlist; some barely mention the date and just call. Both can love the person. Rabi' al-Awwal is the month tradition gives for the birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and Muslims mark it in different ways. Amira's auntie is hosting a mawlid, an evening of poems and stories about his life. Her dad, Yusuf, isn't going. So who's right?
screen: `A PARTY, OR A PHONE CALL.` → `THE MONTH OF HIS BIRTH.` → `AUNTIE'S MAWLID. DAD'S NO.`

segments.voice: Start with what both of them would say. The Qur'an, in Pickthall's words: "If ye love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins." Love, in that verse, isn't only a feeling; it shows up as following. And a report in Sahih al-Bukhari says none of you truly believes until the Prophet is dearer to him than his father, his children and all people. So nobody in this family is arguing about whether to love him. They're arguing about how to show it. Those who hold a mawlid say that gathering to recite poems in his praise, tell his life and send blessings on him is a good way to stir that love; and he himself marked the day he was born, by fasting on Mondays. Those who don't say the companions held no yearly birthday gathering, so the surer way is to keep his sunna every day of the year. Here's what both sides share, worth telling a friend: the month is a reason to read his life, the seerah. A celebration that never opens it misses the point, and so does a refusal that never opens it either. That's love him by following: wherever you land on the party, open the story.
screen: `IF YE LOVE ALLAH, FOLLOW ME.` · `DEARER THAN FATHER AND CHILD.` · `THE MAWLID: STIR THE LOVE.` · `NO MAWLID: KEEP THE SUNNA.` · then, large: `LOVE HIM BY FOLLOWING.`

segments.voice: Say the verse out loud, slowly, in any translation: if you love God, follow me. Then read one short passage of his life, the seerah, from a book you trust, out loud if you can, for as long as the sit runs. One page is enough to begin.
screen: `THE VERSE, OUT LOUD.` · `ONE PAGE OF HIS LIFE.`

segments.voice: Rabi' al-Awwal: the month tradition gives for the Prophet's birth, marked by some with a mawlid and by others with quiet study of his life.
The line for today: love him by following, and open the story, party or no party. Five of fourteen, done.

howItsDone: In Rabi' al-Awwal some Muslims hold mawlid gatherings with poems, stories and salawat, while others keep no special observance. Families on both sides may use the month to read the Prophet's life (seerah) together.

fork.setup: your kid asks: if we don't have a party for the Prophet, does that mean we don't love him? what could you say at dinner?

Rabi' al-Awwal.meaning: a month of the Islamic year

mawlid.meaning: a gathering marking the Prophet's birth

seerah.meaning: the story of the Prophet's life

sunna.meaning: the Prophet's way: what he said and did

sources.quoted: If ye love Allah, follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 15 (none of you believes until I am dearer to him than his father, his children and all people)
Sahih Muslim 1162 (fasting on Monday: the day I was born)
Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (his birth placed in Rabi' al-Awwal)
